units.passage: The instructor may provide additional instructions or limits for any authorized activity. Permitted Actions You may use AI for general questions and support–including concept explanations, study questions, practice problems, ungraded exercises, and exploratory coding–on all work. You may use AI to help develop your submissions only for the specific assignments listed in Authorized Graded Work , subject to any instructions or limits stated for that activity. Prohibited Actions Do not use AI to produce work you submit on any graded assignment that is not listed under Authorized Graded Work . Do not use AI in ways that exceed the stated limits for an authorized graded activity. Do not submit AI-generated work, or lightly edited AI-generated work, as your own when the activity's instructions require work to be independently produced. If an assignment has stricter rules, those rules override this policy for that assignment. Examples Allowed: using AI to explain a concept, generate practice questions, or help you study for a quiz. Allowed: using AI on an ungraded practice exercise or exploratory code that will not be submitted for credit. Allowed: using AI to help produce your submission on a graded assignment if that activity is listed under Authorized Graded Work . Not allowed: using AI to fix a bug or rewrite a proof for you on an assignment that is not listed under Authorized Graded Work . units.passage: feed an AI tool the notes you took from class and ask it to summarize your notes and/or pull out the key points from the lecture. This can help you reflect on what you learned and/or make sure you're understanding what the most important points were. Organizing Thoughts and Ideas When coming up with ideas for a presentation, paper, or research proposal, it can be hard to bring it back to one cohesive idea or see the path to take. You can use AI tools to identify and summarize themes from your thoughts and ideas to get a clear path and move on quickly. Use as Peer Reviewer before submitting Wondering what grade you might get on an assignment? Feed your class rubric and assignment into the AI tool and ask it to grade your assignment based on the rubric. You can go one step further to ask it to give suggestions on how you can improve the assignment to get a better grade. Please note, just because AI gave you a specific grade does not mean that your instructor will give you the same grade. AI is not human and can misinterpret rubrics and expectations. Understanding a grade on an assignment Occasionally, you may be confused about why you received a grade on the assignment, and want immediate feedback. You can use AI tools to get that feedback you want. Feed an AI tool the assignment rubric, your assignment, and your grade, and ask it to explain why you received the grade you did.
